+title: A restore of a root session by id must not make a second instance of a live recorded fork
+---
+## Problem
+
+`RoutedModel.restoreSession(id:)` with the id of a ROOT session restores the root and each recorded fork under it, and then releases the forks (`restoreSessionTree(root:)` with `withForks: true`, `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Recording/SessionRestoration.swift`). Since D205 a fork is a top-level session, so a fork can be live in the same router while a host restores its source by id (for example: the user has the fork open in a tab and opens the recorded source from Recent).
+
+Then the restore makes a second instance of the live fork:
+- `restoredHooks(for:on:)` (`Recording/SessionTreeRestoration.swift`) makes a second `SessionHooks` for the id of the live fork. `start()` replaces `openSessions[forkID]` and posts a `SessionStart(.resumed)` for it. The release runs `end(reason: .released)`, which removes `openSessions[forkID]` of the LIVE fork and posts a `SessionEnd(.released)` for it.
+- `register(_:kind:parentID:)` replaces the live fork in the session directory with the second instance.
+
+When nothing is live, the dispatcher also gets a `SessionStart` and a `SessionEnd(.released)` for each released fork that no caller opened.
+
+^3hxcxee fixed the same cause for a restore by a FORK id (`withForks: false`: the fork alone, its hook parent from the live source). The root path keeps the documented rule that the forks move with the root under `switchingModel`.
+
+## Change
+
+Decide and implement: a root restore by id restores no fork that is live in this router (or restores the root alone, and moves the forks by another way under `switchingModel`), and it fires no hook for a fork that it does not return. Update the doc of `restoreSession(id:)` (the forks paragraph and `switchingModel`).
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] A live fork, then a restore of its source by id: the live fork keeps its hook entry and its directory entry, gets no extra `SessionStart`/`SessionEnd`, and closes with one `SessionEnd`.
+- [ ] Nothing live, a restore of a root by id: hooks fire only for the root.
+
+#d205
\ No newline at end of file

+## Review Findings (2026-11-18 20:34)
+
+> Scope: `review sha HEAD~1..HEAD` — reviewed the diffs only — lines this change added or modified. 4 file(s) reviewed, 2 not reviewed.
+
+> 2 file(s) not reviewed — excluded by an ignore rule:
+> - `.kanban/ (from .reviewignore)` — 2 file(s)
+
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Recording/SessionTreeRestoration.swift:862` `duplication/duplication` — The condition that decides whether a recorded fork moves repeats the test that decides whether the root moves. Both compare the recorded slot and model with the handle. The two checks can drift if one is changed and the other is not. Add one helper on SessionRecord, for example `func differs(slot: ModelSlot, model: ModelRef) -> Bool`, and use it in both places.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Recording/SessionTreeRestoration.swift:866` `duplication/duplication` — The new moveRecordedForks writes the same three index fields that the root restore path already writes: slot, model and context. The two copies can drift apart. A later change to the index fields, such as a new field or a new rule for the context, must then be made in two places. Move the three assignments into one helper that takes a SessionRecord and returns it with the slot, model and context of a RoutedLLM set. Call it from both the root restore path and moveRecordedForks. The two writers may stay separate, because the live session uses updateRecord and the moved fork uses saveLoggingFailure. Only the field assignments need to be shared.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Recording/SessionTreeRestoration.swift:879` `review/orchestrator-check` — `isLive(_:)` makes a suspended fork "not live", so `moveRecordedForks(_:)` writes its `index.md` and its `modelChanged` event. But a suspended session stays in the session directory and keeps its work until `close()` (`RoutedSession.suspend()`). It also keeps its own record in memory, and `updateRecord` saves that record to `index.md` (`recordSubmissionStart`, `recordCompactionCheckpoint`, the archive and unarchive of `RouterSessionDirectory`). The next such write puts the old slot, model and context back in the `index.md` of the moved fork. The events that the suspended session writes after the move also have the old model, after a `modelChanged` event that names the new model. Thus the move of a suspended fork is not durable, and the rule "its session owns its `index.md`" applies to a suspended fork too. Make one rule for each fork that the session directory holds: do not move it on disk, or move it through its live session (its `updateRecord`) so that the record in memory and the `index.md` agree.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Recording/SessionRestoration.swift:233` `review/orchestrator-check` — The doc of `switchingModel` says that a live fork "does not move, because its session owns its `index.md`" and that "a fork that the host suspended moves". A suspended fork also has a session that owns its `index.md` (see the finding on `isLive(_:)`). Make the doc agree with the rule that the fix of that finding sets.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/ModelSwitchRestoreTests.swift:388` `review/orchestrator-check` — `moveRecordedForks(_:)` is a new write path, but the new tests examine only `record.model` of the fork. No test examines that a moved fork gets exactly one `modelChanged` event with the new slot and model, that its `index.md` gets the new slot and context, or that a live fork gets no `modelChanged` event. Add tests for these writes (`modelChangedEvents(of:)` of the `Workspace` helper reads the events).
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Recording/SessionRestoration.swift:272` `review/orchestrator-check` — This call is the only production call of `restoreSessionTree`, and it now always gives `withForks: false`. The `withForks: true` path of `restoreSessionTree` (the default value `true` of the parameter, the guard on `rootNode.parentId`, the walk into `node.children`, and the walk in `requireClaimable`) is now reached only from tests. Production code that only tests reach is dead code. Remove the `withForks: true` path and move the tests that use it to `restoreSession(id:)`, or give the path a production caller.
